A technique list is never complete, and: A technique list is never complete, and the hardest puzzles are made tae beat onything on it. Sae when aw thir come up empty, the tutor settles ane cell by tryin its candidates oot, says plainly that's whit it has done, and carries on reasonin fae there. It aye reaches the end o a puzzle, and it never pretends a lookup wis a deduction.
The Y-wing with the pivot holding one ca:
The Y-wing wi the pivot haudin ane candidate mair. Look for a cell wi exactly three candidates, say {1,4,7}, that can see twa twa-candidate cells - ane {1,7} and ane {4,7}.

Noo aw three o them can be 7, and ane o them maun be. Sae a cell has tae see aw three for 7 tae be ruled oot o it, no juist the twa pincers - which in practice means it sits in the same box as the pivot and on a line wi a pincer.

Fewer eliminations than a Y-wing, and easier tae miss for the same reason: the pivot disnae stand oot.
Work digit by digit rather than square b:
Wark digit by digit raither than cell by cell. For ane unit, write doon whaur each missin digit could still gang. Then look for {0} digits whase lists atween them cover only {1} cells.

Thae {2} digits hae tae fill thae {3} cells, sae everythin else in them can be scored oot - which aften produces a naked single in ane o them or a naked pair across twa o them on the spot.

This is the ane folk find hardest, because there is naethin tae see whan ye look at the cells: they still hae plenty o candidates. The pattern is in the digits.

Look along one row, column or box for sq:
Look alang ane row, column or box for cells wi juist a few candidates left. Tak {0} o them and pool their candidates. If the pool has exactly {1} digits in it, thae {2} digits are spoken for: they hae tae gang in thae {3} cells in some order, even though ye cannae yet say which goes whaur.

That's eneuch. Every ither cell in the unit can gie thae digits up, and it's usually ane o thae cells that then becomes a single.

The cells dinnae aw need the same candidates - {2,7}, {2,9} and {7,9} is a perfectly guid triple, and is the ane fowk miss.
Every sudoku with one answer can be solv: Every sudoku wi ane answer can be solved by reasonin; guessin is never needed and rarely helps. Thir are the weys o reasonin this app can recognise and explain, easiest first. Whaur ane o them applies tae the puzzle ye hae open, it'll show ye every place it does.
